name: Autosomal Dominant Diffuse Palmoplantar Keratoderma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Autosomal Dominant Diffuse Palmoplantar Keratoderma

criteria.description: Presence of diffuse, symmetric hyperkeratosis on palms and soles
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Skin biopsy showing epidermal hyperplasia with orthokeratotic hyperkeratosis
Identification of pathogenic variant in keratin gene (e.g., KRT1 or KRT9)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Diffuse palmoplantar keratoderma plus either positive family history or genetic confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Histopathology and genetic testing support diagnosis but are not mandatory.

laboratory: Skin biopsy showing orthokeratotic hyperkeratosis and epidermal hyperplasia
Negative fungal cultures unless secondary infection present
imaging: Not routinely indicated; imaging may be used to assess complications such as osteomyelitis if infection occurs
genetic: Pathogenic variants in KRT1 or KRT9 genes detected by molecular genetic testing
other: Family pedigree analysis consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

distinguishingFeatures: Prominent nail dystrophy with thickened nails
Mutations in different keratin genes (KRT6, KRT16, KRT17)

redFlags: Rapid progression of hyperkeratosis with ulceration
Signs of secondary infection including purulence and systemic symptoms
Development of constriction bands (pseudoainhum) threatening digit viability
